question: A manufacturing client wants a Claude-based quality-inspection assistant that repeatedly analyzes the same reference specification documents alongside new inspection reports throughout the day. The client's stated goal is to reduce redundant token spend on the unchanging reference material while keeping individual inspection turnaround fast. Which architectural choice best serves this efficiency and cost goal?
options: A) Re-upload the full reference specification as plain text in every single request to guarantee the model always has the latest version
B) Move the entire workload to the Message Batches API so all inspection reports are processed together once per day
C) Increase the effort parameter to xhigh on every inspection request so Claude reasons more thoroughly each time
D) Use prompt caching so the unchanging reference specification is cached and reused across requests, cutting cost and latency
correct_answers: D) Use prompt caching so the unchanging reference specification is cached and reused across requests, cutting cost and latency
explanations: Re-uploading the full reference document in every request is the exact redundant-token pattern the client wants eliminated, and it neither reduces cost nor improves turnaround.
Batch processing trades same-day turnaround for cost savings on non-urgent work, which conflicts with the client's requirement to keep individual inspection turnaround fast throughout the day.
Raising the effort parameter increases reasoning depth and token usage per request, which adds cost rather than reducing the redundant token spend the client wants to cut.

Correct. Prompt caching is designed exactly for this pattern: providing Claude with recurring background context, such as an unchanging reference document, so subsequent requests reduce both cost and latency instead of reprocessing the same content each time.
